Why RGLD?
It offers the best overall balance of quality, risk profile, growth optionality, and relative valuation among the group right now.
• Business model advantage: As a pure royalty and streaming company, RGLD delivers high-margin exposure to gold (and some silver/copper) without the operating risks, cost inflation, or capital intensity that miners like Agnico Eagle (AEM) face. Margins routinely sit near or above 80% EBITDA, the cost structure is extremely lean, and cash flow conversion is strong. This is the same attractive model shared by WPM and FNV.
• Track record and shareholder returns: Since the start of 2000 it has delivered roughly 16% annualized total returns—solid long-term compounding. It also has one of the best dividend growth histories in the precious metals sector (25+ consecutive years of increases, ~15% CAGR since 2000, and membership in the S&P High Yield Dividend Aristocrats). The payout remains well-covered with room to grow.
• Portfolio and growth: The company has meaningfully expanded and diversified through recent acquisitions (including Sandstorm), lengthening reserve life and adding producing and development assets. It still retains embedded growth and optionality from existing streams/royalties while maintaining a strong balance sheet and liquidity for further deals or capital returns (dividends + buybacks).
• Valuation edge: Among the pure royalty/streaming peers, RGLD currently trades at a noticeable discount to both Wheaton (WPM) and Franco-Nevada (FNV) on metrics such as P/E and EV/EBITDA. AEM looks cheaper on absolute multiples, but that discount largely reflects higher operational risk as a traditional miner. RGLD sits in a sweet spot—cheaper than the other high-quality streamers without sacrificing the lower-risk model.
Brief comparison of the alternatives
• WPM: Excellent scale and growth profile, but it often commands the highest premium valuation of the three streamers.
• FNV: Outstanding quality, diversification (including some energy), and consistency, yet it typically trades at a richer multiple.
• AEM: Attractive on pure valuation and a strong gold producer, but it carries the full suite of mining risks (costs, operations, geopolitics) that the royalty model is designed to avoid.
In short, RGLD combines the superior risk-adjusted economics of the royalty/streaming model with a more reasonable entry point than its closest peers and a proven record of compounding returns and rising dividends. That combination makes it my single pick from this group.

Elemental Royalty Corp reported Q2 2026 financials.
The main highlights: 
Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025:
Revenue: $23.8M (+127%)
GEOs: record 5,248 (vs. 3,184)
Net income: $3.6M (vs. $0.16M)
Cash: $74.2M as of June 30, 2026
For the first half of 2026, Elemental sold 10,231 GEOs (a record) and produced revenue of $48.1 million. 
For 2026, the company is still targeting guidance of 17,000-21,000 GEOs.
Elemental’s $239 mil Vizsla Royalties acquisition should close in Q3, giving the company a strong silver-gold NSR in Mexico. 
The Q2 dividend was declared, at a $0.03/share, with an option to receive it in Tether Gold.
The company began a share buy back in Q2, repurchasing $2 million worth of shares.

Franco Nevada Corp posted Q2 2026 financials.
The highlights:
Revenue: $580.9M (+57% YoY)
GEOs sold: 132,405 (+18% YoY)
Operating cash flow: $482.5M (+12% YoY)
Available Capital: $4.3B as of June 30, 2026
Cash on hand: $1.01B 
Franco posted new half year records for every major metric: revenue $1.23B (+67%), Adjusted EBITDA $1.12B/$5.82 per share (+63%), net income $822.6M/$4.27 per share (+80%).
This record period is downstream of higher metals prices as well as contributions from newer assets like Côté Gold, Casa Berardi, Valentine, Porcupine
For Q3 the company is looking forward to the resumption of streams from its Cobre Panama royalty, which was 25% of profits when in production in 2023. Franco expects ~23,100 gold oz and ~265,000 silver oz total from the program.
The company is still on target to hit the upper half of its 2025 GEOs guidance of 510,000-570,000 oz, mostly thanks to stockpile deliveries from Cobre. 
Franco also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.44/share, payable September 24, 2026.

➡️ Do I believe the commodity is going higher?

2. STAGE
Explorer → Developer → Producer → Royalty
➡️ Earlier = more upside and more risk.

3. ASSET
Grade • Size • Mine life • Infrastructure • Jurisdiction
➡️ Is it actually a good deposit?

4. LEVERAGE
➡️ If metal price rises 50%, how much can profits/NPV rise?

5. MONEY 💰
Cash • Debt • Burn rate • Capex • Financing needed
➡️ Can they reach the next milestone without destroying shareholders?

6. MANAGEMENT
➡️ Have they built mines / created value before?

7. VALUATION
Market cap ÷ production / reserves / resources / NPV
➡️ What am I paying compared with peers?

8. CATALYST 🚀
Permitting • Construction • Resource growth • Production • M&A
➡️ What could make the market revalue it?

9. POSITION SIZE
2% = speculative
5% = meaningful
8%+ = high conviction / high consequence

⭐ FINAL QUESTION

“If I'm right, how big can it get?
If I'm wrong, how much can I lose?”

Quality + leverage + valuation + position sizing = survival + upside.

Attributable GEOs: record 5,255 (+256%)

Here’s is a 25 year monthly price chart of silver overlaid with the monthly S&P500 price and with two indicators, relative strength, RSI, at the top and distance from moving average, DFMA (36 month simple moving average) at the bottom. RSI is a momentum indicator and DFMA is a valuation indicator. In late January when silver peaked intraday at $122, the RSI reached a 25 year high of 93 while the DFMA reached at 25 year high of 172%.

The subsequent ~6 month correction took the silver price down 55% to $54.74 before rebounding over the last two weeks to $64.68. The monthly RSI, while no longer in nosebleed territory, is at 59. The DFMA, at 59% is higher than it’s been for about 90% of the past 25 years.

What these indicators tell us is on a historical basis, silver is still significantly overbought and hardly ripe for a strong, sustained rally. In addition, there is meaningful overhead resistance as everyone who bought silver from mid-December to mid-June is underwater and many of them will be looking to get out “whole”.

I expect the silver price to be volatile and whipsaw its way to a modest gain over the next year. I would not be surprised to see silver retest the July lows.

The first question I’m sure everyone wants to as is why would I pick copper for stronger price appreciation than silver or gold when its RSI, 69, is higher than either and its DFMA, 38%, is higher than gold’s?

To answer that we have to look at the price history. While gold and silver are perhaps coming out of corrections after near blow off top rallies, copper has been slowly, steadily trending higher and clocked a new ATH in the past week. Gold and silver’s big rallies are behind, copper’s rally is in front of it. Put another way, gold and silver have significant overhead resistance, copper has none.

Copper broke out of a 19 year base late last year and I believe its rally is just getting started. In copper’s last big rally, from late 2001 to early 2006, copper rose 525%, the RSI peaked at 93 (the highest of the past 25 years) and the DFMA had a 2-1/2 year period north of 40% also peaking at a 25 year high of 120%.

In the past week the government in Chile announced 2026 copper production would be below 2025 levels. Consumers in the U.S. and Asia hold billions of ounces of silver that could come onto the market at the right price, no consumers hold any copper.

I think the copper price can easily double over the next 12 months.

text:
Oil, #1.

Oil is in an 18 year basing pattern and I’ll be the first to admit the oil price 25 year monthly chart doesn’t scream “buy oil”. There is an obvious wedge pattern but the price squeeze which tends to lead to break outs is at least 2-3 years away. The RSI is a neutral 53 and the DFMA is near neutral at 12%. The low DFMA does indicate significant price appreciation is possible but like other valuation metrics, it’s not a timing tool.

So why is oil my top pick for price appreciation when the charts don’t suggest it? For that we have put on our fundamentals hat and look at oil supply and demand. We’re all familiar with the thesis of a decade plus of under investment in sustaining capital in the oil patch. Rick Rule estimates the bill for that comes due in 2028 or 2029 (which the wedge pattern on the chart nicely backs up); however, the near total closure of the Straight of Hormuz (SOH), partial closure of the Bab Al-Mandab Straight and the shut in of ~10,000,000 bbl/day of Iranian and GCC production is going to dramatically accelerate that timeline.

For the past 5-1/2 months since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran the world has been burning through what were clearly massive oil inventories and strategic reserves, reserves which in the end, are finite. When do global reserves reach such a low point that the price response accelerates? I don’t know but I believe it is far less than 12 months.

More significantly I don’t believe the flow of oil and other goods through the SOH will ever return to normal and certainly not in the next 12 months. I think the Iranians have concluded this is the best chance they’ve had in 47 years to reduce the U.S. presence and influence in the region. And Donald Trump knows if he walks away, TACOs, history will pin a giant L is for Loser on his legacy. Losing a war with Iran has far greater negative consequences for the U.S. than the losses in Vietnam Nam, Iraq or Afghanistan. None of them had the capability to become the dominant regional power broker, Iran does. Trump will not TACO.

So inventories drain until there’s an actual supply crunch and price will respond. How high can price go? On a CPI (spare me the CP lie comments) adjusted basis, the 2008 ATH price of $147 in 2026 dollars is $223. Separately we can look at the gold/oil ratio, currently near the high end of the past 25 years. If it was to mean revert, at a constant gold price, oil could trade as high at $240/bbl. If the ratio traded to the low end of that past 25 years, well, that’s four digits.

I’ve written a calendar entry for 15 August 2027 with Friday’s closing prices of the four commodities and I’m looking forward to a year from now to see how they perform and to stock price gains on all of our commodity investments.

Sounding the alarm: Norwegian billionaires are fleeing to Switzerland – 'deeply concerning'
"Unfortunately, I think that ship has sailed when it comes to getting people to return home."
Nikolai Astrup is a member of the Norwegian political party Høyre
More and more wealthy Norwegians are moving to Switzerland.
And this development is now prompting Nikolai Astrup, a member of the conservative party Høyre, to sound the alarm.
This is reported by Norwegian TV 2.
Astrup fears that Norway has already lost "something that will be very difficult to regain."
"Unfortunately, I think that ship has sailed when it comes to getting people to return home. Perhaps a few will move back if we establish a competitive tax level. However, the priority must be to prevent more people from leaving, and this applies particularly to those who are tasked with building the jobs of the future," Nikolai Astrup told TV 2.
"The flight of capital and talent that we have witnessed in recent years is deeply concerning for Norway," he continued.
Astrup describes the ongoing trend as "frightening."
According to a previous tax assessment, as many as 32 billionaires relocated from Norway during the course of 2022, Norwegian media outlet E24 writes.
That figure has only risen since then, reports Norwegian TV 2.
And they have taken immense fortunes with them.
This is money that would have been subject to taxation had it remained in Norway.
One of the primary drivers behind this trend is reportedly the Norwegian wealth tax.

The following might piss off some people: I asked AI if Technical analysis statistically beats market, buy/hold: Statistically speaking, most academic studies show that traditional technical analysis does not beat the market over the long term. What Research Shows
Efficient Markets: Stock prices already reflect all public info. Past trends hold no hidden value.Random Walk: Price changes look random day to day. You cannot easily forecast them with charts.
Why People Still Use It
Behavioral Biases: People see patterns that are not really there, called pareidolia.
Self-Fulfilling Prophecies: If enough traders buy at a certain chart line, the price goes up briefly.
Short-Term Trades: It may work for quick day trading with strict risk rules, but not for long investing. [1, 2, 3, 4]
